title: Coxon resignation — reaction layers

nodes.label: Jacob Coxon
nodes.act: Resigns from Anthropic, forfeits equity, and posts that the companies are racing to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.
nodes.ev: Jacob Coxon, an Anthropic safety researcher, resigns and posts publicly: “I resigned from Anthropic today… Neither company is acting responsibly.”

tweet.text: I resigned from Anthropic today. I spent the last three years doing pretraining research at both OpenAI and Anthropic. Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives. More thoughts below.
tweet.author: Jacob Coxon

refs: NBC News — the internal Slack post first

known: Spent three years on pretraining research at both OpenAI and Anthropic.
Forfeited his equity in order to resign and speak publicly.
Announced internally on Slack before posting publicly.
Reported to have coordinated with AI-policy organisations before resigning, after saying he worked with no third parties.
dossier.risk: Stated position: neither OpenAI nor Anthropic is acting responsibly, and both are “racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.” He paid equity to say it.

nodes.label: Dario Amodei
nodes.act: Publishes “We Must Pace the Frontier,” proposing embedded third-party evaluators such as METR with employee-like access.
nodes.ev: It follows the resignation and the reaction to it.

tweet.text:

Anthropic is unilaterally committing to the first of these steps. We’ll provide third-party evaluators with permanent, employee-level access to our…
tweet.author: Dario Amodei

refs: “We Must Pace the Frontier” — the essay
Zvi Mowshowitz — the most detailed independent reading
nodes.caveat: The essay page carries no dateline. The 12 September date is confirmed by the timestamp on the announcement post below, not by the essay itself.

known: CEO of Anthropic. Published “We Must Pace the Frontier” proposing a three-part slowdown plan.
Committed Anthropic unilaterally to the first step: permanent employee-level access for third-party evaluators.
Named METR as an example evaluator, without METR having sought the role.
dossier.risk: Four dated claims are on file from the essay, tracked to resolution dates:
claims: A self-improving swarm could be capable of taking over the entire internet within 6–12 months
AI has advanced drastically faster since roughly summer 2026, driven by AI building the next generation
Interpretability improvements are possible in 1–2 years with focused effort
A 3–5 year window exists to execute chip restrictions
dossier.cost: Moderate. A unilateral commitment binding his own company, made in public.
